key_insight: LoViF 2026 introduces PhyScore, the first challenge and unified metric framework for jointly assessing perceptual quality and physical/temporal fidelity of videos generated by 2D and 4D world models. It shows that perceptual metrics alone miss crucial failures in dynamics, conditioning consistency, and physical plausibility.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap in evaluation by providing a standardized benchmark and metric for holistic quality assessment of generated videos—covering perceptual quality, physical plausibility, temporal coherence, and consistency with input conditions—across both 2D and 4D generation settings.
method: Organize a public challenge (LoViF 2026) where participants submit metrics that jointly predict four dimensions: perceptual quality, physical plausibility, temporal coherence, and conditioning consistency (PhyScore).

Provide a curated dataset of world-model-generated videos (2D and 4D), multi-dimensional human and/or synthetic annotations, and an evaluation protocol that combines per-dimension scores into a unified leaderboard metric.
Release baselines, evaluation code, and leaderboard infrastructure to compare metrics, analyze failure modes, and promote reproducible evaluation of dynamics-focused generation.
impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to reliably detect when generated dynamics are visually plausible but physically or temporally incorrect, improving benchmarking, model selection, and downstream use in simulation, robotics, and AR/VR. Standardized multi-dimensional scoring accelerates progress toward physically consistent generative models.

paper_title: LoViF 2026 The First Challenge on Holistic Quality Assessment for 4D World Model (PhyScore)
